confirmed: Read the entire markdown conversion, including Appendices A-D, and independently checked the numerical claims against PDF text. The local PDF has 53 pages and its title page says Updated: 24th May 2026; the title-page Latest Version link points to arXiv 2409.08379 (PDF p. 1).

The title and three authors match the form (PDF p. 1). Crossref metadata for DOI 10.2139/ssrn.4684662 has the same title and authors and a 2024 posted date; only its metadata was checked, not the SSRN full text (https://api.crossref.org/works/10.2139/ssrn.4684662).

The observational design_class entries, observational context_class and core=no are supported. The outcomes concern actual code contributions classified by new functionality or maintenance; there is no randomized people study or measured between-person idea diversity (PDF pp. 10-15, Sections 3-4.1; p. 18, Section 4.3; p. 26, Section 5.4.1; pp. 51-53, Appendices C-D).

Random selection in the annotation exercise concerns commit messages; the human experts annotate existing commits rather than being assigned AI assistance on a creative task (PDF p. 14, Section 3.3.2; p. 52, Appendix C). No fewer-than-50-person experiment is present.

The main corpus has 1,187 matched Python/R package pairs and over 620,000 commits; the temporal-control corpus has 273,000 Python commits in the methods; the Rust/Haskell corpus has 1,373 matched pairs and approximately 314,000 commits. The top-2,000 package sampling descriptions and pre-Copilot inactivity exclusion are supported (PDF pp. 11-12, Section 3.2). These are not people counts.

The form correctly preserves the source discrepancy between October 2019-October 2022 in Section 3.2 and October 2019-December 2022 in the Introduction (PDF pp. 11 and 5). The temporal-control windows are 2016 Q2-2018 Q4 and 2020 Q2-2022 Q4 (PDF p. 18, Section 4.3; p. 19, Table 3 note). The Introduction also says 272 thousand historical commits, whereas Sections 3.2 and 4.3 say 273,000, the value used in the form (PDF pp. 5, 12 and 18).

Copilot used Codex and was selectively available for Python/Rust rather than R/Haskell; the paper dates its language-support treatment to October 2021 and its model upgrade to June 2022. Individual adoption is not established by availability (PDF p. 4 and footnote; p. 10, Section 3.1; p. 24, Section 5.3.2; pp. 31-32, Section 6.3).

The contribution definitions are correct: positive net additions of function definitions identify substantive commits; the alternative classifier is GPT-4o and distinguishes Code Development from Maintenance (PDF pp. 12-15, Sections 3.3-3.3.2; pp. 51-53, Appendices C-D).

S1-O1 and S1-O2 coefficients, standard errors, significance marks and observation counts match Table 4 Panel A: new functions 0.800*** (0.190), 0.626*** (0.188), 0.600*** (0.172); no new functions 6.016*** (0.761), 4.870*** (0.806), 4.226*** (0.787); observations 29,050 / 24,739 / 24,739 (PDF p. 21). The Table A1 numbers 2.51 and 8.49 match, subject to the timing-label correction (PDF p. 38).

S1-O3 and S1-O4 coefficients, standard errors, significance marks and observation counts match Table 5 Panel A: Code Development 1.472*** (0.257), 1.270*** (0.266), 1.105*** (0.253); Maintenance 2.299*** (0.371), 2.023*** (0.391), 1.873*** (0.376); observations 29,050 / 24,739 / 24,739 (PDF p. 22).

S1-O5 matches Table 3: 6.816*** (0.892), 5.496*** (0.941), 4.894*** (0.907). Section 5.1 explicitly reports 39.55%, 31.89% and 28.40%, and the treated-group pre-treatment mean of 17.235 commits per quarter (PDF p. 19).

The triple-difference numbers match exactly: Table A2 main terms 0.919*** (0.206) / 0.626*** (0.188), interactions 4.979*** (0.653) / 4.244*** (0.697); Table A3 main terms 1.474*** (0.258) / 1.270*** (0.266), interactions 0.822** (0.267) / 0.753** (0.280). Both tables report 58,100 / 49,478 observations, not people (PDF p. 38).

All numerical claims and the substantive-versus-incremental ordering in one_line_finding are supported by Table 3, Table 4 Panel A, Table 5 Panel A and Tables A2-A3 (PDF pp. 19, 21, 22 and 38). These are raw commit-count effects and percentages, not standardized creativity effects.

The same PDF contains the stated appendix material: Table A1 summary statistics, A2-A3 triple differences and A4-A10 robustness (PDF pp. 38-40); Appendix B includes the replication and combined-language analyses (PDF pp. 41-50); Appendix C gives annotation methods and Appendix D function detection (PDF pp. 51-53). This is an original observational paper, not a synthesis; no meta-analytic pooled estimates need extraction.
summary: No randomized people study was found; the observational classification and reported effect estimates are supported. Corrections address the mislabeled Table A1 statistics, matched-pair wording, unresolved assignment/count/statistics fields, and missing outcomes for the two additional analyses.
